title: [GR-31840] [GR-31681] Allow native-image shared libs to be built on module-path and fix resource bundle lookup.

timeline.body:
- Removes the undocumented native-image.properties property `ImageIncludeBuiltinModules`. It was previously needed for building truffle-based images. Cleaning up class-init for Java 11+ make the existence of  `ImageIncludeBuiltinModules` obsolete. (I.e. if there is truffle, it's classes are subject to class-init)
- Fix implementation of ResourceBundle access. Packages that contain ResourceBundles are opened up in their respective modules prior to accessing them from the image-builder. This also fixes https://github.com/oracle/graal/issues/3404
- Add support for building shared library images where the `--module-path` is used.
- Build native-image-agent and native-image-diagnostics-agent via `--module-path` and test the shared objects in `mx hellomodule`
@gilles-duboscq please have a look at the changes in `sdk/mx.sdk/mx_sdk_vm_impl.py` and `sdk/mx.sdk/mx_sdk_vm.py` if that makes sense to you.
Can a library have a "main module"? or should this rather be an attribute of `LauncherConfig`?

reply.body:
I took inspiration from `mx_sdk_vm_impl.GraalVmNativeImage.__init__`
```python
svm_support = _get_svm_support()
if svm_support.is_supported():
    deps += self.native_image_jar_distributions
```
Previously I just had
```
deps = self.native_image_jar_distributions
```
here, but seeing the code from `mx_sdk_vm_impl.GraalVmNativeImage.__init__` made me suspect that `svm_support.is_supported()`should also be used here.

The reason why I need to specify the dependencies is that I need to run the `NativePropertiesBuildTask` after the jars are made into proper modules so that using
```python
build_args += image_config.get_add_exports(set(export_deps_to_exclude))
```
in `mx_sdk_vm_impl.NativePropertiesBuildTask.contents` works reliably.

I think it would be worth explaining why that dependency is added in a comment.

Regarding the check I think `GraalVmNativeImage` checks `_get_svm_support().is_supported()` because if that's true then the native image will be built which requires the input jars to exist. That's because those projects can either build native images or just shell launchers.
On the other end, `GraalVmNativeProperties` only exists if SVM is supported anyway so i don't think this check adds much. However a version check would remove the dependency when it's not necessary (on 8)

> I think it would be worth explaining why that dependency is added in a comment.

Will do.

> However a version check would remove the dependency when it's not necessary (on 8)

Makes sense. I will add that.
Fixed in fdae21edcc566b12bd00e989302c56d86217c478

reply.body:
> what distribution is both on the jvmci/boot classpath and part of the jars of a launcher/library?

Right, alternatively I could fix why we need this is the fist place.

Which is that currently the `native-image.properties` generated by `mx_sdk_vm_impl.NativePropertiesBuildTask.contents` have a `ImageClasspath/ImageModulePath` that contains all the transitive jars from the image builder itself. In case of using the module system this is not allowed and the jars from the image builder itself need to be filtered out (hence the filtering in `com.oracle.svm.driver.NativeImage#addImageModulePath`). This way I could also get rid of all the filtering related code in `com.oracle.svm.driver.NativeImage#addImageModulePath`.
OK, thanks for the explanation. I'll let you decide what's the best approach there.

off-topic:
I am a little confused by the concept of known_missing_jars. Based on the comment above their definition it seems they are optional runtime dependencies. Shouldn't the variable then be called something like `optional_runtime_depedencies`, `optional_runtime_deps` or `optional_svm_runtime_deps` ? When I read known_missing_jars, it's not clear to me what the purpose is and it evokes the thought that there is probably some sort of implementation defect involved and this variable is a patch over it.

reply.body:
The whole "concept" of `_known_missing_jars` seems very ad-hoc. I'm just using it here as it makes sense to get rid of `--add-exports` that would be hurtful if the respective jars are in fact missing. If there would be an optional jar that would actually need `--add-export`s we would be in trouble.

> it's not clear to me what the purpose is and it evokes the thought that there is probably some sort of implementation defect involved and this variable is a patch over it

I agree. but cleaning this up (introducing proper handling of optional jars) is beyond the scope of this PR. It would be an entire PR on its own ... seems someone is volunteering to look into this :wink:

timeline.body: Clever idea to allow the user to specify the module from which the bundle should be loaded. However, I would put the parsing into the caller and have the module as an optional argument. For the command-line options, it makes sense to have this parsing, but for the config file, a new key-value pair separate from the bundle name might be more expressive. And the classloader support shouldn't be aware of the nuances of locale configuration parsing. However, this is more of a `todo` for me to implement it once this gets merged.

timeline.body:
Hi @olpaw ,

With this check in place jar files including resource bundles in .properties file format at their root are not supported. Such an example is [org.eclipse.yasson](https://github.com/eclipse-ee4j/yasson/tree/master/src/main/resources) (seen failing in https://github.com/quarkusio/quarkus/issues/18305).

Going through [ResourceBundle's Javadoc](https://docs.oracle.com/en/java/javase/11/docs/api/java.base/java/util/ResourceBundle.html) I was not able to find any mention/guidance on avoiding adding ResourceBundles to the root of jar files, so I am wondering if this is something we should relax on GraalVM.

Thanks

reply.body: @zakkak Yes we should probably add fallback code for that to support that. Please create an issue for me.
